mainTopic: The time for the nighttime קריאת שמע, why the משנה opens with the evening, and what its wording teaches about eating תרומה
overview: The opening משנה of מסכת ברכות asks from when we may say the nighttime קריאת שמע. It answers: from when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה. There are three opinions about the end time. רבי אליעזר says the end of the first watch, the חכמים say חצות, and רבן גמליאל says עמוד השחר. רבן גמליאל explains that the חכמים' חצות is only a fence to keep people from sin, and that the מצוה itself lasts until dawn. The גמרא then asks why the משנה asks 'from when' without first teaching the מצוה, and why it starts with the evening. It answers that the תנא builds on the פסוק 'בשכבך ובקומך', or on the creation story, where evening comes first. Next, the גמרא asks why the משנה did not simply say 'when the stars come out.' It answers that the wording also teaches that a כהן may eat תרומה at nightfall even before bringing his כפרה, as a ברייתא learns from 'ובא השמש וטהר'. The amud ends by asking how we know this פסוק means the sunset and the day clearing; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The opening question and the start time for the night שמע
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks from when we may say the evening קריאת שמע. It answers: from the time the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when do we say שמע at night? From the time the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens מסכת ברכות with a question about the earliest time to say the nighttime שמע, and gives the answer right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not give a clock time. It points to a familiar event, the moment כהנים begin eating תרומה, and uses it as the starting point. Everyone in the משנה agrees on this start time; the argument that follows is only about the end time.

keyTerms.meaning: From when? (from what time)
Saying the שמע
In the evening, at night
Priests, descendants of אהרן
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים to eat

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is giving a START time here, not an end time. All the arguing in the next lines is about when the time ENDS.

phrases.english: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
From the time that the kohanim go in
to eat their terumah.
phrases.notes: תרומה is the holy portion of produce given to the כהנים, which they may eat only when they are ritually pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the מסכת; nothing comes before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time for the nighttime קריאת שמע begins when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the time ends at the end of the first watch
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that the nighttime שמע may be said only until the end of the first watch of the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until the end of the first watch. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the first opinion about the END time: רבי אליעזר says it ends with the first watch of the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night is divided into sections called 'watches.' רבי אליעזר limits the time to the first of them, which is the earliest end time in this משנה. The words 'דברי רבי אליעזר' tell us this is his personal view, which others are about to dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'watch,' one section of the night
The first
Until the end of

phrases.english: Until the end of the first watch.
phrases.notes: The night is split into sections called 'watches'; this means the end of the first one.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד סוֹף הָאַשְׁמוּרָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the end time to the start time given in step 1, according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the nighttime שמע may be said only until the end of the first watch.

steps.title: The חכמים: the time ends at midnight
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר and say the nighttime שמע may be said until חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: until חצות (midnight).
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion about the end time: the חכמים give more time than רבי אליעזר, up to חצות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The start time stays the same; only the end time changes. The חכמים stretch the deadline past the first watch, all the way to the middle of the night.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the group of rabbis disagreeing here
Midnight, the middle of the night

phrases.english: And the Sages say: Until midnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר's end time in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the nighttime שמע may be said until חצות.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: the time lasts until dawn
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל gives the longest time: the nighttime שמע may be said until עמוד השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: until עמוד השחר (dawn) comes up.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion about the end time: רבן גמליאל says you have the whole night, until dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three end times, from shortest to longest: end of the first watch (רבי אליעזר), חצות (חכמים), and עמוד השחר (רבן גמליאל). רבן גמליאל treats the whole night as the time for the nighttime שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor used for the leader (נשיא) of the Jewish people
Dawn, the first light in the sky
That it comes up (rises)

steps.whatToRemember: Three end times for the nighttime שמע: רבי אליעזר = end of first watch; חכמים = חצות; רבן גמליאל = עמוד השחר.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Until dawn comes up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, longest end time, disagreeing with both רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן גמליאל, the nighttime שמע may be said until עמוד השחר.

steps.title: The story of רבן גמליאל's sons coming home late
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל's sons came home late from a wedding feast and had not yet said שמע. He told them that if dawn had not come, they still must say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once his sons came home from a wedding feast. They told him: we have not said שמע. He told them: if dawn has not come up yet, you are obligated to say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real-life story showing רבן גמליאל ruling according to his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons were clearly past חצות, or they would not have needed to ask. רבן גמליאל did not say 'too late.' He told them they are still obligated, because for him the time lasts until dawn. The story shows his opinion was put into practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an actual event
A house of feasting, a wedding celebration
Obligated, required
We have recited

phrases.english: There was an incident: his sons came back from a wedding feast,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא קָרִינוּ אֶת שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: they said to him: We have not recited Shema.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִם לֹא עָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
phrases.english: He said to them: If dawn has not come up,
you are obligated to recite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבן גמליאל's opinion from step 4 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: רבן גמליאל's ruling that the nighttime שמע may be said until עמוד השחר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real event in which רבן גמליאל told his sons, after a late wedding feast, that they must still say שמע if dawn had not come.

steps.title: A general rule: 'until midnight' really means until dawn
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל adds a wider rule: in every place the חכמים said 'until חצות,' the מצוה truly lasts until עמוד השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only this did they say. Rather, anything the חכמים said 'until חצות,' its מצוה lasts until עמוד השחר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains to his sons that the חכמים' 'until חצות' does not mean the מצוה truly ends at חצות; it actually lasts until dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes how we read the argument in step 3. רבן גמליאל is saying the חכמים agree that the real מצוה lasts all night. Their 'until חצות' is an earlier deadline they set, not the true end. He also says this is a general rule that goes beyond שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only this
Anything that they said, every case where they said
Their מצוה, the real time the מצוה can be done

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, the חכמים' 'until חצות' is an earlier deadline they set. The real מצוה, both for שמע and wherever they said 'until חצות,' lasts until עמוד השחר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים hold the מצוה truly ends at חצות. רבן גמליאל explains that even for them, the מצוה itself continues until dawn.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a three-way argument into something closer to agreement between the חכמים and רבן גמליאל about the real end of the מצוה, and it applies this to every 'until חצות' rule.

phrases.english: And not only this did they say,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים ״עַד חֲצוֹת״,
phrases.english: but rather, anything the Sages said 'until midnight,'
its מצוה lasts until dawn comes up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא כָּל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים עַד חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבן גמליאל's words to his sons, explaining how his ruling fits with the חכמים' 'until חצות.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever the חכמים said 'until חצות,' the מצוה itself may be done until עמוד השחר.

steps.title: Two more examples where the מצוה lasts until dawn
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל backs up his general rule with two examples from the קרבנות: burning fats and limbs on the מזבח, and eating קרבנות that are eaten for one day. Both may really be done until עמוד השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning the fats and limbs on the altar may be done until dawn. All offerings that are eaten for one day may be eaten until dawn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל is giving examples to prove his rule from Step 6. In each case the real מצוה lasts until עמוד השחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רבן גמליאל said that wherever the חכמים said 'until חצות,' the מצוה truly lasts until dawn. Here he gives two examples from the בית המקדש of night-time מצוות whose Torah limit is dawn. The one-day קרבנות are a case where the חכמים set an earlier deadline of חצות, but the מצוה itself still lasts until dawn.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning on the מזבח (altar)
The fats and limbs of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
קרבנות that may be eaten only on the day they are brought, plus the night after

phrases.english: The burning of fats and limbs [on the altar],
their מצוה lasts until dawn rises;
and all [offerings] that are eaten for one day,
their מצוה lasts until dawn rises.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶקְטֵר חֲלָבִים וְאֵבָרִים, מִצְוָתָן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples for the general rule stated in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבן גמליאל's rule that every 'until חצות' really means until עמוד השחר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The laws of burning fats and limbs on the מזבח, and of eating one-day קרבנות

steps.title: Why the Sages set midnight as the deadline
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: if the מצוה truly lasts until dawn, why did the חכמים say 'until חצות'? The answer is to keep a person far from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did the Sages say 'until midnight'? To keep a person far away from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks why the חכמים gave an earlier deadline, and answers that it is a protective fence. This closes the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים were not arguing about the Torah's real time limit. They made an earlier deadline so that people would not push off the מצוה and end up missing dawn. So חצות is a fence the חכמים set up, while dawn is the true Torah limit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a phrase that sets up a question
To distance, to keep far away
A sin or transgression

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, the Torah's limit is עמוד השחר. The חכמים' 'until חצות' is a protective fence so that people won't put off the מצוה too long.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the חכמים believe the Torah itself ends the מצוה at חצות. In this explanation, חצות is an extra safety line they added; the מצוה itself still lasts until dawn.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, לָמָה אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים ״עַד חֲצוֹת״
phrases.english: If so, why did the Sages say "until midnight"?
In order to keep a person far away from sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לָמָה אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים עַד חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the חכמים set an earlier time if the real limit is dawn, as Steps 6-7 showed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים' deadline of חצות is a fence to keep people from missing the מצוה; the true limit is עמוד השחר.

steps.title: How can the משנה ask 'from when' without first teaching the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. It asks what the תנא is building on when he opens with 'From when?' It sounds as if we already know there is a מצוה to say שמע, but this is the very first משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the תנא basing himself on, that he asks 'From when?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the first word of the משנה, 'מאימתי.' This sets up the answer that comes in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking 'from when' assumes we already know there is a מצוה to say שמע at night. But the משנה never told us that. So the גמרא wants to know where the תנא got this from.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
The sage who teaches the משנה
Literally 'where is he standing?', meaning what is he basing himself on

phrases.english: Gemara
Where is the tanna standing,
phrases.notes: He means: asking 'from when' assumes we know there's a מצוה, so where did the תנא learn that?

phrases.english: that he teaches "From when?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion by looking at the opening word of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What earlier source the תנא relies on in assuming there is a מצוה of the nighttime שמע

steps.title: Why does the משנה start with the evening and not the morning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second question. Why does the משנה teach the evening שמע first? It should have started with the morning שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: why does he teach the evening first? Let him teach the morning first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the משנה, which starts with ערבית. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we would expect the day to come first, so starting with the evening seems strange. The גמרא pushes: 'Let him teach the morning first!' This is a second difficulty added to the question of Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: And further, used to add another question
What is different? Why treat this case differently?
The evening, here the evening שמע
The morning, here the morning שמע
First, at the beginning

phrases.english: And further: what is different,
that he teaches about the evening first?
Let him teach about the morning first!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּתָנֵי בְּעַרְבִית בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difficulty about how the משנה opens.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the משנה, which teaches the evening שמע before the morning שמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Morning seems like the natural place to start, so opening with the evening needs an explanation.

steps.title: The תנא is building on the פסוק 'when you lie down and when you rise'
steps.stepSummary: One answer solves both questions. The תנא relies on the פסוק 'בשכבך ובקומך.' The פסוק already teaches the מצוה, and it mentions lying down (night) first. So the משנה asks when the time for the 'lying down' שמע begins: from when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is relying on a פסוק, as it is written: 'when you lie down and when you rise.' This is what he is teaching: when is the time for the שמע of lying down? From when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both questions together. The תנא is basing himself on the פסוק, which already gives the מצוה and puts night first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Question one is answered because the מצוה is already known from the פסוק, so the משנה only needs to ask 'from when.' Question two is answered because the פסוק says 'בשכבך' (lying down, at night) before 'ובקומך' (rising, in the morning), and the משנה follows that order. The גמרא then reads the משנה as asking about the time of the 'lying down' שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: He is standing on a פסוק, meaning he is basing himself on a verse
When you lie down and when you rise, the source for saying שמע at night and in the morning
Lying down, meaning the nighttime

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is built on the פסוק 'בשכבך ובקומך.' That is why it can ask 'from when' right away, and why it starts with the nighttime שמע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of how the משנה works: it often takes a מצוה from the Torah for granted and only explains the details. It also follows the order of the פסוק.

phrases.english: The tanna is basing himself on a verse,
as it is written: "When you lie down and when you rise."
And this is what he is teaching:
The time for reciting the Shema of lying down, when is it?
From the time the priests go in to eat their teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא אַקְּרָא קָאֵי, דִּכְתִיב: בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both questions from Steps 9 and 10 with one source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a פסוק that both teaches the מצוה and sets the order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה had no basis for assuming the מצוה, and that it should have started with the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא relies on 'בשכבך ובקומך': the מצוה is already known from the פסוק, and the פסוק mentions night first.

steps.title: A second answer: evening comes first in the creation story
steps.stepSummary: Another reason the משנה starts with the evening שמע is that the תנא learns from the creation of the world, where evening is listed before morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that the תנא learns from how the world was created. The פסוק says: 'And there was evening, and there was morning, one day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of why the משנה starts with the evening שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer pointed to the פסוק 'בשכבך ובקומך.' This answer points to the creation story instead. There, evening is named before morning, so a day begins at night. That makes it natural to begin with the evening שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say': brings a second, different answer
He learns it (from a source)
The creation of the world

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that, in הלכה, the day begins with the night before it.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
he learns it from the creation of the world,
as it is written:
"And there was evening, and there was morning, one day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question from step 10, in place of the פסוק used in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source: evening comes before morning in the order of creation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The morning שמע should come first, since the day seems to begin in the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the creation story lists evening first, the day starts at night, so the evening שמע comes first.

steps.title: Challenge: a later משנה puts morning first
steps.stepSummary: If evening always comes first, why does a later משנה list the ברכות of the morning שמע before those of the evening שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the later משנה that teaches: 'In the morning you say two ברכות before שמע and one after it. In the evening you say two before it and two after it.' It should have taught the evening first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the משנה always puts evening first, by pointing to a later משנה that starts with the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה put evening first because evening comes first, either from the פסוק or from creation. But a later משנה in the same פרק lists the morning ברכות first. If evening really comes first, that later משנה is out of order.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': if your reasoning is right, then there is a problem
The later part of a משנה or פרק
'Let him teach': the משנה should have said it this way

phrases.english: If so,
the later clause, which teaches:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in the same פרק, not the next line of our משנה.

phrases.english: "In the morning one says two blessings before it
and one after it;
in the evening one says two before it
and two after it",
let it teach the evening one first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'evening first' principle from steps 11 and 12 by pointing to a later משנה that does not follow it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that the משנה lists evening before morning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If evening comes first, the later משנה about the ברכות should also start with evening. It starts with morning, so the order looks inconsistent.

steps.title: Answer: once on the morning topic, he finished it
steps.stepSummary: The תנא did begin with evening and then moved to morning. Since he was already on the morning topic, he explained the morning details first and then went back to the evening details.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא started with the evening שמע, then taught the morning שמע. While he was on the morning שמע, he explained everything about the morning, and only then explained the evening matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining how the order of the פרק flows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Evening still comes first: the פרק opens with the evening שמע. After that, the פרק moved on to the morning שמע. When the topic of ברכות came up, the תנא was still on the morning, so he finished the morning details before going back to the evening ones. The order is about the flow of teaching, not a break from the 'evening first' principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Opened, began with
And then, afterward
While he was standing at, while he was already dealing with
Matters, details

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה begins with the evening שמע, either because of 'בשכבך ובקומך' or because of the creation story. The later morning-first order is just the תנא finishing the topic he was already on.

phrases.english: The תנא opened with the evening one,
and then taught the morning one;
while he was standing at the morning one,
he explained the matters of the morning,
and then explained the matters of the evening.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Flow of teaching: the order depends on which topic the תנא was already on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later משנה shows the תנא does not really put evening first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרק opens with evening. The morning-first order later on comes only from finishing the morning topic once it had started.

steps.title: Why not just say 'when the stars come out'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה. The כהנים eat תרומה once the stars come out, so why didn't the משנה simply say 'from when the stars come out'?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'From when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה.' Now, when do the כהנים eat תרומה? From when the stars come out. So let the משנה just say: 'From when the stars come out'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the exact wording of the משנה's start time. It asks why the משנה used a roundabout description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא points out that the time the כהנים eat תרומה is simply the time the stars come out. If both mean the same time, the simpler wording would have been clearer. So why did the משנה bring in the כהנים and תרומה at all? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, after all': introduces a known fact as the basis for a question
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which he may eat only when he is טהור
When the stars come out, nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: 'אמר מר' here does not bring in a new sage. It just quotes our own משנה again so the גמרא can look at its wording.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: Here 'the Master' is just our משנה being quoted again.

phrases.english: "From the time the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה."
Now, the כהנים,
when do they eat תרומה?
From the time the stars come out.
So let it teach: "From the time the stars come out"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִים לֶאֱכוֹל בִּתְרוּמָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'why evening first' discussion and opens a new question about the משנה's wording for the start time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'משעה שהכהנים נכנסים לאכול בתרומתן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The time the כהנים eat תרומה is the same as the time the stars come out. So the משנה should have used the simpler wording, and the longer description seems unneeded.

steps.title: The wording teaches when כהנים eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה used the long phrase about כהנים to teach, in passing, that כהנים eat תרומה from when the stars come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching us something extra along the way: when do כהנים eat תרומה? From the time the stars come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. The משנה chose the longer wording on purpose, so it could slip in an extra lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'from when the stars come out' would only have taught the time for שמע. By saying 'from when the כהנים go in to eat their תרומה,' the משנה teaches the time for שמע and also the time for eating תרומה. The extra words are not wasted. They carry a second הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter taught in passing, along the way
It teaches us (a new point)
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים, which they may eat only when pure
When the stars come out (nightfall)

phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing:
When do priests eat teruma?
From the time the stars come out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 about the משנה's long wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra wording teaches an added הלכה in passing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase about כהנים seemed like an unnecessary, roundabout way of saying nightfall.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase was chosen to also teach that כהנים eat תרומה from when the stars come out.

steps.title: A second lesson: the atonement offering does not hold him back
steps.stepSummary: The wording also teaches that a missing כפרה does not stop a כהן from eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the משנה also teaches us that the atonement offering does not hold him back from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second hidden lesson in the משנה's wording. This sets up the proof from a ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהנים eat at nightfall and says nothing about bringing a כפרה first. So a כהן who has finished his purification may eat תרומה that night, even before he brings his offering. That is the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement offering, brought by some impure people to finish their purification
Does not hold back, is not required first

phrases.english: And this teaches us
that the atonement offering does not hold him back.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן may eat תרומה even before he brings his offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן דְּכַפָּרָה לָא מְעַכְּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second lesson learned from the same wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A further הלכה hidden in the wording
steps.terutzMaskana: Not having brought the כפרה yet does not prevent eating תרומה.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves it from the verse 'And the sun sets and he is pure'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that sunset is required before eating תרומה, but the atonement offering is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And the sun sets and he is pure.' The setting of his sun holds him back from eating תרומה, but his atonement offering does not hold him back from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the lesson from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes eating תרומה depend only on the sun setting. It does not mention bringing an offering. So the ברייתא concludes that sunset is required, and the כפרה is not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the sun sets and he is pure' (the פסוק about when an impure כהן may eat)
The setting of his sun, the sunset after his immersion
Holds him back, prevents him

phrases.english: As was taught in a baraita: "And the sun sets and he is pure":
the setting of his sun holds him back
from eating teruma,
but his atonement offering does not hold him back
from eating teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the lesson stated in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That the כפרה does not prevent eating תרומה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the פסוק 'ובא השמש וטהר'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule: a כהן who has immersed may eat תרומה once the sun sets, even before he brings his offering.

steps.title: How do we know the verse means sunset and a clear sky?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that 'ובא השמש' means sunset and that 'וטהר' means the day has cleared.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that 'and the sun sets' means the setting of the sun, and that 'and he is pure' means the day has become clear?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how the ברייתא reads the פסוק. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's proof only works if 'וטהר' is about the day clearing at nightfall. If it meant something else, the proof that the כפרה is not needed might fall apart. So the גמרא asks for a basis for this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
'And he is pure': here read as 'and it is clear'
The day has cleared, full nightfall

steps.confusionAlert: 'וטהר' can sound like it is talking about the person becoming pure. The ברייתא reads it as the day becoming clear, and that reading is exactly what the גמרא is now checking.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this "and the sun sets"
means the setting of the sun,
and this "and he is pure" means the day has cleared?
phrases.notes: Literally 'the day is pure.' He means the light is fully gone and the stars are out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ברייתא of step 18 reads the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that 'ובא השמש וטהר' refers to sunset and the clearing of the day, and not some other meaning
